slides.kicker: STUDENTS, IN YOUR HOSTEL OR LIBRARY
title: two-word AI
commands
slides.sub: Save these. They work in ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude today.

slides.name: *Understand* it
slides.line: When to use: the chapter made no sense and class is tomorrow.

rows.v: Plain words, like for a Class 8 student
One everyday example of the idea
Shows two ideas side by side
Tells you why before the how
Where this topic fits in the subject
Lists the words you must know
Explains it like something from daily life
Next level, once the basics click

slides.catch: It can explain wrongly too. Check your textbook.

slides.name: *Study* it
slides.line: When to use: the week before an exam, right after you finish a chapter.

rows.v: Asks you questions on the topic
Turns notes into question and answer pairs
Questions shaped like a real exam paper
After a quiz, lists topics you got wrong
Splits your syllabus across the days left
Short ways to remember lists and formulas
One-page notes from a long chapter
Plays examiner and asks viva questions

slides.catch: Paste your syllabus first, or it guesses what's in it.

slides.name: *Write* it
slides.line: When to use: before you hit send on an email, SOP or assignment.

rows.v: Same message in fewer words
Paste your old writing; it copies that style
Turns a casual line into office tone
Same text, written in Hindi
Corrects spelling and grammar mistakes
Swaps hard words for easy ones
Sounds friendlier, less stiff
Fixes the language, not your point

slides.catch: Check your college's AI rules before you submit.

slides.name: *Organise* it
slides.line: When to use: your notes are a mess, or a project has too many parts.

rows.v: Puts messy info into rows and columns
Breaks a task into numbered steps
Long paragraph into short points
Events in date order, history or projects
A branching outline of the topic
Sorts a mixed list into categories
Turns your tasks into a day schedule
A tick-box list you can follow

slides.catch: Check it didn't drop any of your points.

slides.name: *Decide* it
slides.line: When to use: choosing a course, a laptop or an internship offer.

rows.v: Three or more choices, not just one
Good and bad side of each choice
Stops listing, makes one clear choice
Drops the polite padding, says it straight
Orders your choices from best to worst
What happens if it goes wrong
Pushes back on what you already think
Only options that fit your money

slides.catch: It doesn't know your life. Add your marks and budget.

slides.name: *Check* it
slides.line: When to use: before you submit, share or believe an answer.

rows.v: Points out errors in your work
Asks you questions before it answers
Flags the parts it isn't sure about
Rechecks claims; turn on web search
Shows each step of a maths answer
Redoes the sums to catch errors
Names where its facts come from
Spots gaps in your answer or plan

slides.box: MY FAVOURITE: Ask first. It stops the AI guessing. Copy this: "Ask first. Ask me 3 questions before you answer, then wait. My question: [type it here]"
slides.catch: Sources can be made up. Open every link.

slides.title: The *catch.*
items: The AI just reads your words and follows them.
ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude each word answers differently.
Fact check still means you open the source yourself.
Your textbook and teacher still come first.

slides.title: Save this. Send it to *your roommate.*
slides.who: Who types full paragraphs to ChatGPT, still gets bad answers.
slides.text: and I'll DM you all 48 as one copy-paste card
